findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public endpoint reachable from the internet rather than confining it to the VPC. Combined with a database holding application data and the admin master user, this substantially widens attack surface.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume and its snapshots, leaving stored data unencrypted at rest.

The master password is supplied from var.password and passed directly into the instance and into EC2 user_data; the value is stored in plaintext in Terraform state and is not sourced from Secrets Manager/SSM. The master username is also the hard-coded privileged 'admin' account.

The MySQL parameter group applied to this instance does not set require_secure_transport, and the PHP client connects with mysqli_connect without TLS options, so application-to-database traffic can be unencrypted cleartext.

The EC2 user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or attacker on the host (and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute), exposing the database master credentials in cleartext.

No metadata_options block is defined, so IMDSv1 remains enabled on an internet-facing web server that also renders user-supplied input; SSRF or local compromise can trivially retrieve the instance profile credentials for the over-privileged catalog_app_role.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's root volume — which stores the dbinfo.inc file containing the database master password — may be created unencrypted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the public web server. Compromise of the instance yields full control of S3 data, EC2 (including privilege escalation via new instances/roles) and all RDS databases in the account.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control path from a compromised database tier.

findings.issue_category: network control bypassed by public endpoint
findings.description: This security group is the only network boundary for the database, but because the RDS instance is publicly_accessible its endpoint resolves publicly; any later widening of the ingress rule immediately exposes MySQL to the internet with no additional segmentation in depth.
